tokens.name: material-canvas-shadow
tokens.description: Rung 0 (canvas): the shadow that separates it from what is behind.

tokens.name: material-canvas-scrim
tokens.description: Rung 0 (canvas): the minimum scrim opacity needed for text on this rung to clear the contrast floor.

tokens.name: material-canvas-opaque
tokens.description: Rung 0 (canvas): the opaque substitute used under prefers-reduced-transparency and where backdrop-filter is unsupported.

tokens.name: material-inset-tint
tokens.description: Rung 0.5 (inset): the tint over what is behind it. The recessed well inside a card: the explanatory note a Callout draws inside the reading it annotates, and the track a RangeBar lays its range along. Its fill sits below the card fill in both themes, so the well reads as carved into the card rather than lifted off it. In light it is neutral-100, one step under the white card, which is where a Callout already sat. In dark it is a value between the page and the card, below the card so the well is a recess and above the page so a Callout used on its own is still visible.

tokens.name: material-inset-tint-alpha
tokens.description: Rung 0.5 (inset): how opaque that tint is.

tokens.name: material-inset-scrim
tokens.description: Rung 0.5 (inset): the minimum scrim opacity needed for text on this rung to clear the contrast floor.

tokens.name: material-inset-opaque
tokens.description: Rung 0.5 (inset): the opaque substitute used under prefers-reduced-transparency and where backdrop-filter is unsupported.

tokens.name: material-sheet-tint
tokens.description: Rung 3 (sheet): the tint over what is behind it. A bottom sheet or side panel the reader can dismiss by dragging. Its tint is now near opaque, so the panel lands close to the card colour and a white control inside it no longer floats above a greyer surface. What keeps the covered page recognisable is the scrim around the panel rather than the page reading through the panel, because at this opacity very little of the page shows through the tint.

tokens.name: ease-spring-snap
tokens.description: Direct manipulation only: a switch the reader just flipped, a segmented control, a pressed button settling. It overshoots by 1.5%. That is enough to feel physical but not enough to look playful. The 1.5% is the largest overshoot in the system but not the only one: `spring-settle` overshoots by 0.88%. Only `spring-calm` and `spring-sheet` reach their target without passing it.

tokens.name: duration-spring-snap
tokens.description: Settle time for the spring-snap spring, measured from its own parameters.

tokens.name: ease-spring-settle
tokens.description: The workhorse for chrome: popovers, tooltips, menus, chips appearing and disappearing.

tokens.name: duration-spring-settle
tokens.description: Settle time for the spring-settle spring, measured from its own parameters.

tokens.name: ease-spring-calm
tokens.description: A health value that changes while it is already on screen: a bar re-filling from one reading to the next, a dial travelling between two values the reader has already been shown. Never a first paint and never a first reveal. A value arrives at its final figure, with no count-up, no dial sweep and no line drawing itself in (health/motion-in-health-ui rule 2). Slightly overdamped (zeta just over 1) so it never overshoots and never bounces.

tokens.name: duration-spring-calm
tokens.description: Settle time for the spring-calm spring, measured from its own parameters.

tokens.name: ease-spring-sheet
tokens.description: Large surfaces travelling a long distance: sheets, dialogs, full-screen pushes. Overdamped, because a sheet that bounces at the top of its travel reads as a dropped object.

tokens.name: duration-spring-sheet
tokens.description: Settle time for the spring-sheet spring, measured from its own parameters.

tokens.name: ease-standard
tokens.description: Non-spring transitions where a spring would be overkill: colour, opacity, border. Fast out, slow in.

tokens.name: ease-enter
tokens.description: Something arriving from off-screen or from nothing. Decelerating, because an arrival should feel like it is coming to rest.

tokens.name: ease-exit
tokens.description: Something leaving. Accelerating and shorter than its enter, because a reader does not need to watch a dismissal finish.

tokens.name: duration-instant
tokens.description: State change with no travel: hover tint, focus ring, checkbox tick.

tokens.name: duration-fast
tokens.description: Small elements moving a small distance.

tokens.name: duration-base
tokens.description: The default for chrome that is not spring-driven.

tokens.name: duration-slow
tokens.description: Layout change: a list reflowing, a card expanding.

tokens.name: duration-deliberate
tokens.description: The ceiling on a transition a reader is waiting on, such as a first-run reveal or a consent sheet, where the point is that the reader notices. No such transition may exceed it. A looping placeholder period, like the skeleton shimmer, is bounded instead by its iteration count, so a single sweep of it may run longer.

tokens.name: duration-shimmer
tokens.description: One sweep of a loading placeholder's sheen. This is a period, the time for the sheen to make one pass across the bar, and not a travel time. At 1600ms the movement reads as calm rather than as urgency, which the first motion rule requires of anything that is not a value the reader controls. Its consumer pairs it with a finite iteration count so the total motion stays under the five seconds at which WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.2 engages.
